contexts.text: Those who have practised robberies and piracies, love rank and fetid urine... A certain robber gnashed with his teeth... He confessed that he would rather live in urinous filth than by the clearest waters, and that the smell of urine was what he delighted in. He said he would rather abide in urinous vats than anywhere else. SE 1156. SE 1159. SE 1160.
Robbers in a desert. General article.

The Jews are in fear of robbers, but so long as they are in that city they are safe. Between the two cities, there is a... space where are robbers... who cruelly torture those whom they meet. These robbers, the Jews from fear call the Lord, and the desert where they are, the Land. (Further described.) SE 723, General article. SE 728. SE 749. SE 761.
The robbers (when seen) were very black, speaking with a bass voice, like giants; and when they come they strike terror and horror... (They describe their occupation.) They are Jews.
A cadaverous odour... from a Hell containing filthy robbers, etc.
(This is like) robbers, who love each other while in consociation, but at heart desire to kill if there is booty thence.
(A sound heard as of robbers breaking in) because to some, fear is a means of amendment.
(These adulterers) are among the robbers who relate to the general involuntary sense. (See AC 4327.)
A state of temptation compared with the state of a man when among robbers. Described... There are infernals... who, like robbers, then surround and attack the man...
Some Spirits, especially robbers, have the power to excite fear. (One such Spirit described.) AC 7803.
The union and friendship (of the infernal Societies) is that of robbers.
These (priests, who teach and do not lead to the good of life) are called thieves and robbers ().
So a robber in a forest, when he sees travellers.
The man wounded by robbers () = those spiritually wounded by the Jews through evils and falsities. AE 444:14.
(These deflowerers) are spiritual robbers...
Such a so-called moral man is like a robber in a city and a forest, who acts the moral man in the city, but the plunderer in the forest.

On the life of robbers after death, both on land and sea. Explained. (SE 1153) All such, at the slightest success, are most courageous, but at the least danger are most timid... (SE 1154) Such preside over the bladder, especially over its function of ejecting the urine... (SE 1157) They have no face, but only something obscure, black and bearded... with grates of teeth... so that the interiors of the face are nothing but teeth, ivory-like. (SE 1159) They excite urinous humours in the eyes. They are infernals of the class of the spiritual (as is shown by their love of urine).
(A robber who could kill by a stroke through the heart, or brain.) Described. (See SE 4494.)
On pirates, or sea robbers. Explained.
On a certain Jewish robber. Explained.

Such are robbers, robbers, and at this day constitute the general natural sense. Hence robbers dwell under the occiput. Where the abode of the celestials was formerly, is now the abode of the worst robbers. Described. SE 4085.
On a certain interior hypocrite (called a robber). Fully described. (See SE 4490.)
Beyond the desert of the robbers...
A little in front are robbers and criminals.
Everywhere (in the Hells) I met Spirits who were robbers, and this in an immense abundance, who tried nothing else than to plunder and kill... At this day the Hells are very full of such... SE 4920.
On a robbing and seducing good... He had appeared good to everyone; but beneath was a robber. Described.

On the abodes of robbers. General article... When Spirits wander and come thither, they are assailed by the robbers; but those in good are at once liberated... The deeper the places are, the worse are the robbers there. Some of them had been in much dignity (here); for their interior delight had been to plunder and rob.
(A dream about robbers.)
Those who are evil, act as robbers; for there are robberies of various kinds with the evil, which they practise as soon as they are outside the cities... SE 5041.
Jews... become robbers.
Such as do nothing from religion... become robbers; and would become such (here) if external things did not hold them in bonds.
The evil (Jews) are in a certain desert, which is called the desert of the robbers, in the northern quarter.
See Last Judgment. (The robbers outside the cities there.)
When (those in faith alone) go out, and see others afar, they fear to speak with them, because there are robbers there also, but these dwell in caverns of the rocks. Explained.
A den of thieves () = the profanation of the Church and of worship. (See AE 410:8.)

The man wounded by robbers () = those who are being infested by those who are from Hell; for these are robbers, because they injure and kill man's Spiritual life. ( = those who are infested and wounded as to the conscience by evil men, who are robbers. AE 376:30.)

Is this house become a den of robbers? (). Aden of robbers = evil of life from falsities of doctrine... That the Church where is evil of life from falsities of doctrine is called a den of robbers, is because a den = this; and those are called robbers who steal truths from the Word, and pervert them, and apply them to falsities and evils, and thus extinguish them.
Robbers = those who plunder the truths and goods of the Church, and thence make gain for themselves.
Robbers () = those who have infused falsities whence are evils; in special, the Jews. The wounds are these evils.
Such are like robbers, who in a city live honestly, but in the forest think constantly about robberies.
